To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
folic acid supplementation in mice leads to liver injury, which is more severe when the mice are genetically deficient for MTHFR.
high folic intake reduces MTHFR levels, leading to a pseudo-MTHF R deficiency that causes fatty liver in mice.
folic acid supplementation in MTHFR-deficient mice causes a pseudo-MTHF deficiency that leads to fatty liver disease and altered lipid metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of folic acid in the liver, the major organ for folate homeostasis.
the impact of folic acid intake and the interaction of this intake with genotype.
